title: Credit expirations & upgrade prompt experiment to improve PLG conversion
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: Redwood offers free credits to new signups and trial accounts, but conversion to paid customers is lower than expected for enterprise signups. Existing experiments changed credit size in isolation; we lack systematic data on expiry windows, in-product upgrade prompts, and enterprise-specific messaging.

Goal: Increase PLG-to-paid conversion and lead qualification for enterprise accounts while minimizing margin erosion. Measure lift in trial-to-paid conversion rate, paid ARR per converted account, and retention at 90 days.

Hypotheses:
1) Longer credit expiry (60 days vs 30 days) increases meaningful usage and raises conversion rate for mid-market/enterprise prospects.
2) Tailored in-app upgrade prompts (quota/usage thresholds + enterprise CTA to contact sales) at behavioral triggers increase demo requests and contract conversions.
3) A small increase in initial free credits for high-value product flows (embeddings, long context gen) reduces early churn without materially increasing short-term cost.

Experiment design:
- Arms: Control (current credits: 1000 tokens, 30d expiry, current CTA), Arm A (1000 tokens, 60d expiry), Arm B (1500 tokens, 30d expiry), Arm C (1500 tokens, 60d expiry + contextual enterprise upgrade prompts).
- Target cohorts: new self-serve orgs with >5 seats or flagged enterprise email domains. Randomize at org-level.
- Size: minimum 1,200 orgs total (300 per arm) to detect +2.5ppt conversion at 80% power.
- Duration: 8 weeks active window + 90d follow-up for retention.

Instrumentation & metrics:
- Primary metric: trial->paid conversion within 90 days (org-level).
- Secondary metrics: demo/contact-sales rate, MRR expansion at 180 days, cost-per-converted-account (estimated incremental token spend), average daily active users (DAU) during trial, churn at 90 days.
- Events to log: credit_allocated, credit_consumed (tokens per request), credit_expired, upgrade_prompt_shown, upgrade_prompt_clicked, contact_sales_requested, billing_migration_completed. Analytics dashboard: https://our-analytics.company.com/dashboards/PLG-CREDIT-5512 (placeholder).

Rollout plan:
1) Finalize experiment config with Eng (ENG-2034 for server-side expiry enforcement; ENG-2101 for UI CTA).
2) Legal & Security review for enterprise messaging and data handling (LEGAL-92).
3) Run closed beta on 5 pilot accounts for 2 weeks to validate event fidelity.
4) Gradually ramp to full experiment over 3 days with 25/50/100% exposure steps.

Gating & success criteria:
- Prior to ramp: pilot instrumentation error rate <1%, upgrade prompt CTR >0.5% in pilots, no critical performance regression.
- Success: statistically significant increase in trial->paid conversion (one-tailed p<0.05) for any experimental arm vs control and acceptable cost-per-conversion (<= 1.5x baseline).

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: Increased credits materially increase token spend. Mitigation: cap per-request token size, monitor real-time spend in Console alerts; abort if spend > 200% projected.
- Risk: Enterprise messaging triggers compliance or security questions. Mitigation: pre-review language with Legal and Security, add FAQ links and pre-baked SSO/KMS info for enterprise leads.
- Risk: Confounding effects from concurrent pricing changes. Mitigation: avoid running other pricing/credits experiments concurrently; coordinate with PM-5400.

Design & Copy notes:
- Upgrade prompt UX should be contextual (usage milestone + clear next steps: 'Upgrade now', 'Talk to sales'). See mockups: https://drive.google.com/mockups/PLG-5512 (placeholder).
- Email follow-ups at 7 days before expiry and at expiry encouraging next steps. Email templates drafted in Confluence: https://confluence.company.com/display/PLG/Credit+Expiry+Emails (placeholder).

Acceptance criteria for Done:
- Experiment deployed and collecting events for full cohort, dashboard showing real-time metrics, analysis notebook with results, recommendations for production rollout or rollback, and decision documented in Confluence.

Notes: This ticket intersects with enterprise contract/security questionnaire work: when upgrade prompts drive sales conversations, Sales/Legal may request updated security questionnaires. Add process to route questionnaire requests to Solutions Engineering and attach standard SAML/KMS diagrams in the campaign assets.
